suggestions.title: "Reviews keep warning about the risk with 5-HTP, like this case report ..."
suggestions.reading: with "MedlinePlus" out: [Human Written, 0%](https://www.pangram.com/history/3881db67-9c63-4207-9928-69655c68e7aa), High, Medium (3 words: "Luckily he recovered."), High, the same as your version with it in ([link](https://www.pangram.com/history/67441215-b92b-4ca5-a6ff-86941d93f7c2)).
suggestions.why: Your version said "like this MedlinePlus case report", but the case report isn't MedlinePlus's: it's Patel and Marzella 2017 on PubMed Central ([the report](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5580516/)). MedlinePlus was the page on what serotonin syndrome looks like, which your version folded in. So the article now says "like this case report", and the MedlinePlus page is linked on your first words, "Serotonin syndrome", where the reader meets the term. I left "Reviews keep warning ..., like this case report" as you wrote it: the reviews do warn, and the case report shows the risk they warn about.
suggestions.advice_note: Keep the fix. If you want MedlinePlus named, say where, and I'll check that wording.

suggestions.title: "In Calabrese, et al (2024), three adults on a ketogenic diet ..."
suggestions.reading: the paragraph: [Human Written, 0%](https://www.pangram.com/history/53b000ed-a200-44af-8eb7-051b992576a1), one window, High, on the first try.
suggestions.why: Your post said Calabrese, et al (2024) "have shown in one study that's part of much broader research that ketones and reduced carbohydrate intake are highly effective for anxiety, depression, and other mental illnesses". The paper is a case series of three adults on a ketogenic diet, all of whom went into full remission of depression and anxiety within 7 to 12 weeks ([the paper](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11182043/)). Three people can't show "highly effective", and it didn't look at other mental illnesses, so the paragraph now says what it found, and keeps your "part of much broader research". It also comes after the step it supports (the ketones), and the paragraph opens on its point: "If your cortisol is normal or low, low ATP signaling in the brain might be what's behind your anxiety or depression."
suggestions.found_by: Reading both of the paragraph's sources before it went in (gate E348), 5 November

suggestions.title: "So I'd trial 20mg of PQQ in the morning to boost ATP ..."
suggestions.reading: in the same check as the card above ([Human Written, 0%](https://www.pangram.com/history/53b000ed-a200-44af-8eb7-051b992576a1)): High.
suggestions.why: Not a change: a question about your argument, which is yours to decide. The mouse study (Wang, Gao and colleagues in JNeurosci, 2025, as [ScienceDaily](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2025/11/251126025315.htm) reports it) found less ATP released by astrocytes in the hippocampus, through a protein called connexin 43, and restoring that protein restored the ATP and the mice's behavior. PQQ helps cells make more ATP. Whether making more means more gets released is your reasoning, not the study's; "I'd trial" already says it's an experiment. I'd keep it as it is.
suggestions.advice_note: Keep it as it is, unless you want to say why making more ATP should help its release.
suggestions.found_by: Reading the mouse study before the paragraph went in, 5 November
